- When sentiment is low (≤0.20) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent price spike is followed by model overshoot (forecast > true +10%), apply downward correction to align with mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 10% of historical mean, adjust forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect underperformance.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.40) and forecast is flat or slightly downward, increase forecast by 1–3% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If forecast and true outcome diverge by >5% in first 5 days of horizon, apply early correction to prevent lagged error amplification.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or declining — cap upward revisions at +3% unless sentiment >0.50.
